   - The call to `__cpuid_entry_get_reg()` in the `kvm_cpu_cap_mask()` function was updated to pass `cpuid.reg` instead of a pointer to `cpuid`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in both files are interconnected as they address the same issue regarding the handling of the `cpuid` parameter. The change in `cpuid.h` to accept a `u32 reg` instead of a pointer allows for a more straightforward access to the register values, which resolves the alignment issues encountered when building with `CONFIG_UBSAN=y`. The corresponding updates in `cpuid.c` ensure that all calls to `__cpuid_entry_get_reg()` are consistent with the new function signature, thereby maintaining the integrity of the code and preventing potential bugs related to pointer dereferencing. Overall, these changes enhance the robustness of the CPUID handling in the KVM module.

Here is the commit message:
KVM: x86: Fix BUILD_BUG() in __cpuid_entry_get_reg() w/
 CONFIG_UBSAN=y

Take the target reg in __cpuid_entry_get_reg() instead of a pointer to a
struct cpuid_reg.  When building with -fsanitize=alignment (enabled by
CONFIG_UBSAN=y), some versions of gcc get tripped up on the pointer and
trigger the BUILD_BUG().

Reported-by: Randy Dunlap <rdunlap@infradead.org>
Fixes: d8577a4c238f8 ("KVM: x86: Do host CPUID at load time to mask KVM cpu caps")
Fixes: 4c61534aaae2a ("KVM: x86: Introduce cpuid_entry_{get,has}() accessors")
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <sean.j.christopherson@intel.com>
Message-Id: <20200325191259.23559-1-sean.j.christopherson@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the use of a pointer to a `struct cpuid_reg` in the `__cpuid_entry_get_reg()` function, which led to issues when compiling with the `-fsanitize=alignment` flag. Certain versions of GCC had trouble handling the pointer, triggering a `BUILD_BUG()` due to alignment constraints. The fix involved changing the function to accept the target register directly, avoiding the pointer dereference that caused the alignment issue.

Here is the patch:
 
 static __always_inline u32 *__cpuid_entry_get_reg(struct kvm_cpuid_entry2 *entry,
-						  const struct cpuid_reg *cpuid)
+						  u32 reg)
 {
-	switch (cpuid->reg) {
+	switch (reg) {
 	case CPUID_EAX:
 		return &entry->eax;
 	const struct cpuid_reg cpuid = x86_feature_cpuid(x86_feature);
 
-	return __cpuid_entry_get_reg(entry, &cpuid);
+	return __cpuid_entry_get_reg(entry, cpuid.reg);
 }
 
 		return NULL;
 
-	return __cpuid_entry_get_reg(entry, &cpuid);
+	return __cpuid_entry_get_reg(entry, cpuid.reg);
 }

```c
u32 reg
switch (reg) {
return __cpuid_entry_get_reg(entry, cpuid.reg);
```
Reason:
The fix involved changing the function to accept the target register directly (`u32 reg`) instead of a pointer to a `struct cpuid_reg`. This avoids the pointer dereference that caused the alignment issue, thus preventing the `BUILD_BUG()` from being triggered during compilation with the alignment sanitizer.
